notes: The NCD lists covered indications but has no explicit non-coverage section, so no case tests an unlisted indication; not-covered cases fail a stated qualifier (severity, last resort, unresponsiveness) or the nonhospital setting conditions. Hyperglobulinemias (including cryoglobulinemia) carry no qualifier. Reviewer to confirm: with no 'all other indications non-covered' clause, a MAC could arguably cover qualifier-failing cases locally; labels here treat a failed stated qualifier as not covered under this NCD.

criteria.text: Plasma exchange for acquired myasthenia gravis
criteria.span: Plasma exchange for acquired myasthenia gravis
Plasmapheresis in the treatment of primary macroglobulinemia (Waldenstrom)

criteria.text: Plasma exchange/plasmapheresis for life-threatening rheumatoid vasculitis only as last resort
criteria.span: Plasmapheresis or plasma exchange in the last resort treatment of life threatening rheumatoid vasculitis

criteria.text: Chronic relapsing polyneuropathy: severe or life-threatening symptoms and failure of conventional therapy
criteria.span: Treatment of chronic relapsing polyneuropathy for patients with severe or life threatening symptoms who have failed to respond to conventional therapy

criteria.text: Scleroderma/polymyositis: life-threatening and unresponsive to conventional therapy
criteria.span: Treatment of life threatening scleroderma and polymyositis when the patient is unresponsive to conventional therapy

criteria.text: SLE: last resort for life-threatening disease when conventional therapy failed
criteria.span: Treatment of last resort for life threatening systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) when conventional therapy has failed to prevent clinical deterioration

criteria.text: Nonhospital setting: physician present at all times during patient care hours
criteria.span: A physician (or a number of physicians) is present to perform medical services and to respond to medical emergencies at all times during patient care hours

criteria.text: Nonhospital setting: all nonphysician services under direct, personal physician supervision
criteria.span: All nonphysician services are furnished under the direct, personal supervision of a physician.

cases.note: Plasma exchange for acquired myasthenia gravis in a hospital outpatient department.
cases.vignette: 71-year-old woman with acetylcholine receptor antibody-positive acquired myasthenia gravis (ICD-10-CM G70.01) with worsening bulbar weakness and dysphagia over 2 weeks despite pyridostigmine and prednisone. A course of five plasma exchange sessions is requested in the hospital outpatient apheresis unit before starting a steroid-sparing agent.

cases.note: Guillain-Barre syndrome is listed without a severity or last-resort qualifier; mild, ambulatory disease is a distractor.
cases.vignette: 67-year-old man with Guillain-Barre syndrome (ICD-10-CM G61.0) diagnosed 4 days ago by clinical findings, CSF albuminocytologic dissociation and nerve conduction studies. He has distal weakness and areflexia but can still walk 10 meters unaided and has normal respiratory function. Plasma exchange as an inpatient is requested.

cases.note: Severe chronic relapsing polyneuropathy (CIDP) that failed IVIG and steroids.
cases.vignette: 69-year-old woman with chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (chronic relapsing polyneuropathy, ICD-10-CM G61.81) now unable to walk without a walker, with severe proximal and distal weakness. She failed to respond to 6 months of IVIG and to high-dose oral prednisone. Plasma exchange in the hospital outpatient department is requested.

cases.note: CIDP with mild symptoms: requires severe or life-threatening symptoms (and failed conventional therapy).
cases.vignette: 64-year-old man with chronic relapsing polyneuropathy (CIDP, ICD-10-CM G61.81) with mild distal paresthesias and minimal foot weakness; he walks normally, works full time and has no respiratory or bulbar involvement. His symptoms did not improve after 3 months of IVIG. Plasma exchange in the hospital outpatient department is requested.

cases.note: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia in a physician-directed clinic meeting all nonhospital-setting conditions.
cases.vignette: 76-year-old man with Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia (ICD-10-CM C88.0) with IgM 6,200 mg/dL, headaches, blurred vision and retinal venous engorgement from hyperviscosity. Plasmapheresis is requested at a freestanding physician-directed apheresis clinic where a physician is on site to perform medical services and respond to emergencies at all times during patient care hours, each patient is under a physician's care, and the apheresis nurses work under the direct, personal supervision of the on-site physician.

cases.note: Nonhospital clinic with no physician present during patient care hours (available by phone only).
cases.vignette: 73-year-old woman with acetylcholine receptor antibody-positive myasthenia gravis (ICD-10-CM G70.01) with worsening generalized weakness despite pyridostigmine and azathioprine. Maintenance plasma exchange is requested at a freestanding infusion and apheresis clinic. Her neurologist oversees her care, but the sessions are run by apheresis nurses, and no physician is on site during clinic hours; the medical director is available by telephone and comes in once a week.

cases.note: SLE with non-life-threatening manifestations (rash, arthritis): not last-resort treatment of life-threatening SLE.
cases.vignette: 66-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus (ICD-10-CM M32.9) with photosensitive rash and inflammatory arthritis of the hands. Kidney function, urinalysis, blood counts and neurologic and cardiopulmonary findings are normal. Her rash and joint pain persisted despite hydroxychloroquine and low-dose prednisone. Plasmapheresis in the hospital outpatient department is requested.

cases.note: Life-threatening rheumatoid vasculitis, but plasma exchange is requested as initial therapy, not as last resort.
cases.vignette: 70-year-old man with long-standing rheumatoid arthritis who developed rheumatoid vasculitis (ICD-10-CM M05.20) with mononeuritis multiplex and mesenteric ischemia, considered life-threatening. He was admitted yesterday and has not yet received any treatment for the vasculitis; the rheumatologist requests plasma exchange to begin today as first-line therapy, with corticosteroids and cyclophosphamide to be considered later if needed.

cases.note: Scleroderma limited to skin and not life-threatening.
cases.vignette: 65-year-old woman with limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (ICD-10-CM M34.1) with skin thickening of the fingers and Raynaud phenomenon. Pulmonary function, echocardiogram, kidney function and blood pressure are normal, with no digital ulcers. Her skin thickening progressed despite 12 months of methotrexate. Plasmapheresis in the hospital outpatient department is requested.

cases.note: Life-threatening polymyositis, but no record of conventional therapy or response.
cases.vignette: 68-year-old man with biopsy-proven polymyositis (ICD-10-CM M33.20) with severe proximal weakness, dysphagia with aspiration and early respiratory muscle weakness, admitted to the ICU. His rheumatologist requests inpatient plasma exchange. The admission note describes his current status but does not state what treatment, if any, he has received for polymyositis or how he responded, and no medication history is included.

cases.note: Nonhospital clinic: physician presence documented, but nothing shows nonphysician services are under direct, personal physician supervision.
cases.vignette: 74-year-old woman with cryoglobulinemia (ICD-10-CM D89.1) causing purpura and progressive neuropathy. Plasmapheresis is requested at a freestanding physician-directed clinic. The clinic's attestation states that a physician is present on site at all times during patient care hours and that each patient is under a physician's care; it says nothing about who performs the apheresis or how the technicians and nurses are supervised, and no other description of the clinic's staffing is provided.
